'''Suresh Chand Jain''' (5 December 1926 – 10 December 2009) was an Indian physicist and director of the [[Defence Research and Development Organization]]. Known for his research in solid state physics, Jain was an elected fellow of the [[Indian National Science Academy]] and [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]. In 1966, the [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards for his contributions to physical sciences.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link – please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:IIT Delhi.JPG|thumb|235px|IIT Delhi]]
S. C. Jain, born on 5 December 1926 in [[Saharanpur]] in the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]], earned an MSc degree in physics in 1949 and followed it up with a PhD in solid state physics from [[Delhi University]] in 1955, carrying out his research at the [[National Physical Laboratory of India|National Physical Laboratory]], Delhi under [[Kariamanickam Srinivasa Krishnan]].<ref name="Biography">{{Cite web |url=http://en.encyclopediaofjainism.com/index.php?title=DR._S._C._JAIN |title=Biography |date=2017 |publisher=Encyclopedia of Jainism}}</ref> Subsequently, he moved to the UK to take up the position of a faculty member at [[University of Leeds]] and worked there until 1958.<ref name="Deceased fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/N79-0340 |title=Deceased fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link – please click ''J'' and select ''SC Jain'' to see details}} On his return to India, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi]] where he served as the head of the department of physics from 1965 to 1968 and as the dean of faculty of science from 1966 to 1969. Concurrently, he worked at his alma mater, the National Physical Laboratory, and held the position of a deputy director during 1965–69, and as the director of ''Solid State Physics Laboratory'' (SSPL) during the period 1969–74. While heading the SSPL, he also held the directorship of the [[Defence Research and Development Organization]] (DRDO). In between, he did visiting professor assignments at [[University of Illinois]], [[Atomic Energy Research Establishment]] and [[Imperial College of London]] (1975–77).<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

Jain died on 10 December 2009, at the age of 83.<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

== Legacy ==
During his doctoral studies, Jain assisted his mentor, K. S. Krishnan, the co-discoverer of the [[Raman Effect]],<ref name="Kariamanikkam Srinivasa Krishnan">{{Cite web |url=http://www.vigyanprasar.gov.in/scientists/KS_Krishnan/KariamanikkamSKrishnan.htm |title=Kariamanikkam Srinivasa Krishnan |date=2017 |publisher=Vigyan Prasar Science Portal |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071223092455/http://www.vigyanprasar.gov.in/scientists/KS_Krishnan/KariamanikkamSKrishnan.htm |archive-date=2007-12-23 }}</ref> on the [[thermal conductivity]] of solids.<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> It was during this time, the duo developed a methodology for the measurement of thermal conductivity in solids at high temperatures<ref name="Conductivities and Emissivities of Metals at High Temperatures">{{Cite web |url=http://eprint.iitd.ac.in/bitstream/2074/4248/1/TH-33.pdf |title=Conductivities and Emissivities of Metals at High Temperatures |last=Tara Chand Goel |date=2017 |publisher=IIT Delhi}}</ref> which was published by them in an article, ''Thermionic Constants of Metals and Semiconductors. II. Metals of the First Transition Group'' in 1952 in ''Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences''<ref name="Thermionic Constants of Metals and Semiconductors. II. Metals of the First Transition Group">{{Cite journal |last=S. C. Jain, K. S. Krishnan |title=Thermionic Constants of Metals and Semiconductors. II. Metals of the First Transition Group |jstor=99091 |journal=Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series A, Mathematical and Physical Sciences |date=1952 |volume=215 |issue=1123 |pages=431–437 |doi=10.1098/rspa.1952.0222|bibcode=1952RSPSA.215..431J |s2cid=97000522 }}</ref> and later explained further by way of another article, ''Determination of thermal conductivities at high temperatures'' in [[British Journal of Applied Physics]] in 1954.<ref name="Determination of thermal conductivities at high temperatures">{{Cite journal |last=S. C. Jain |title=Determination of thermal conductivities at high temperatures |journal=British Journal of Applied Physics |date=1954 |volume=5 |issue=12 |pages=426–430 |doi=10.1088/0508-3443/5/12/302 |bibcode=1954BJAP....5..426K }}</ref> The measurement protocol later came to be known as the "Jain-Krishnan Method".<ref name="Deceased fellow" /> Polar crystals, [[thin films]] and [[semiconductor devices]] are some of the other areas he worked on, and he was credited with developing experimental techniques in these disciplines which are in use around the world.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=483 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize}}</ref> He also contributed to the development of electronic equipment for the military.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999}}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and he published four books viz. ''Recent advances in semiconductors: theory and technology'',<ref name="Delhi1971">{{cite book|author=S. C. Jain|title=Recent advances in semiconductors: theory and technology: proceedings of the International Advanced School on Theory and Technology of Semiconductors, held during April 6 – May 5, 1968 at Indian Institute of Technology, New Delhi|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Fbb6MAAACAAJ|year=1971|page=255|publisher=Hindustan Pub. Corp. (India)}}</ref> ''Nonmetallic crystals'',<ref name="Nonmetallic crystals : proceedings of the international conference on the science and technology of nonmetallic crystals, New Delhi">{{cite book|author=S. C. Jain, L T Chadderton|title=Nonmetallic crystals : proceedings of the international conference on the science and technology of nonmetallic crystals, New Delhi|year=1970|page=335|publisher=Gordon and Breach Science Publ.|isbn=9780677142104|oclc=964077912}}</ref> ''Germanium-silicon strained layers and heterostructures'',<ref name="Germanium-silicon strained layers and heterostructures">{{cite book|author=S. C. Jain|title=Germanium-silicon strained layers and heterostructures|year=1994|page=302|publisher=Academic Press|isbn=9780120145980|oclc=30078949}}</ref> and ''Electronic absorption and internal and external vibrational data of atomic and molecular ions doped in alkali halide crystals''.<ref name="Electronic absorption and internal and external vibrational data of atomic and molecular ions doped in alkali halide crystals">{{cite book|author=S. C. Jain; A V R Warrier, S K Agarwal|title=Electronic absorption and internal and external vibrational data of atomic and molecular ions doped in alkali halide crystals|year=1974|page=51|publisher=National Bureau of Standards|oclc=351740405}}</ref>

Jain was the director of the ''International Advanced School on Theory and Technology of Semiconductors'', an [[Indian Institute of Technology Delhi|Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi)]] program held in April 1968. He chaired the international conference on science and technology of [[Nonmetal (chemistry)|non-metallic]] crystals held at IIT Delhi in January 1969 and was associated with [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] as a member of its solid state commission.<ref name="Biography" /> He was also a member of the editorial boards of journals such as [[Radiation Effects and Defects in Solids]], ''Crystal Lattice Defects and Amorphous Materials'' and ''Journal of Nonmetals'' and was a senior member of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]].<ref name="Deceased fellow" />

== Awards and honors ==
The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded Jain the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1966<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> and the [[Indian National Science Academy]] elected him as a fellow in 1979.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy}}</ref> He was also a fellow of the [[National Academy of Sciences, India]],<ref name="NASI Deceased fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/deceased.htm |title=NASI Deceased fellows |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=9 April 2017 |archive-date=28 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528102550/http://www.nasi.org.in/deceased.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Physical Society of London]], [[American Physical Society]], [[Faraday Society]]<ref name="Biography" /> and [[Institution of Electronics and Telecommunication Engineers]].<ref name="Deceased fellow" />
